patches.value: Choose C from F001. Apply M008 on C to the identity map into Euclidean ℝ^n. It gives a finite real bound on the norm of every point of C. Taking the maximum of that bound with zero and then adding one gives a positive radius strictly larger than all these norms. Each coordinate absolute value is at most the Euclidean norm, so C is contained in the open box of that radius. Thus a positive enclosing radius exists, even if C is empty.

All partial derivatives of u are smooth on ℝ^n×(0,∞). For every x∈ℝ^n,t>0 and j∈{1,…,n}, ∂_t u_j(j,x,t)=v_j(j,x,t). For every x∈ℝ^n,t>0, e_t(x,t)=2u_t(x,t)·u_tt(x,t)+2∑_{j=1}^n u_j(j,x,t)·v_j(j,x,t). The functions e and e_t are smooth on that domain.
